subject.title: Feature Request: Cross-platform migration tool (migrate export/import)

question: Should OpenClaw core own an automated same-product archive import/restore command, or should core stay limited to safer backup export, platform conversion, verification, and manual restore guidance?
rationale: The answer determines the CLI namespace, archive trust boundary, destructive write policy, secret/session portability, and whether overlapping backup/plugin work should proceed in core.

options.title: Define minimal native import contract
options.body: Scope a preview-first core export/import lifecycle with canonical target validation, secret/session policy, rollback/conflict handling, and security-focused tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep restore user-driven
options.body: Evolve `openclaw backup` with platform targeting, archive conversion, verification, and clearer manual restore docs without adding a destructive importer.

options.title: Route optional workflows to plugins
options.body: Keep core limited to missing APIs and let plugin or skill packages own cloud, scheduled, encrypted, or workspace-specific migration flows.

recommendation.title: Define minimal native import contract
recommendation.body: Scope a preview-first core export/import lifecycle with canonical target validation, secret/session policy, rollback/conflict handling, and security-focused tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: gumadeiras already articulated the restore security boundary in the closed exact implementation discussion and is the clearest routing candidate for this decision.
